newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MARINERS ACQUIRE OLIVARES, LIRA FROM TIGERS FOR SANDERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MARINERS ACQUIRE OLIVARES, LIRA FROM TIGERS FOR SANDERS.

text.p: The Seattle Mariners bolstered their pitching staff Friday by acquiring right-handed starters Omar Olivares and Felipe Lira from the Detroit Tigers for right-handed hurler Scott Sanders and two minor-leaguers.
The Tigers, building for the future, received as prospects right-handed pitcher Dean Crow and third baseman Carlos Villalobos from the Mariners.

Olivares was 5-6 with a 4.70 ERA in 22 appearances, including 19 starts, with the Tigers. He has 74 strikeouts and 53 walks while ranking second in the American League with two shutouts and fifth with three complete games.

In eight major-league seasons with St. Louis, Colorado, Philadelphia and Detroit, Olivares is 42-45 with a 4.39 ERA in 201 games. He should join Randy Johnson, Jeff Fassero and Jamie Moyer in the Seattle rotation.

"We were able to add a couple of good arms to our pitching staff. Olivares and Lira are experienced pitchers that have had success," said Mariners manager Lou Piniella. "Olivares will move right into our rotation and Lira will go into the bullpen."
Lira compiled a 5-7 mark and 5.77 ERA with a shutout in 20 outings, including 15 starts, with Detroit. In three seasons with the club, he went 20-34 with a 5.03 ERA in 89 appearances.

The Mariners acquired Sanders from the San Diego Padres in the off-season for Sterling Hitchcock. He started the season in the starting rotation, but lost all four starts and was relegated to the bullpen. Overall, he is 3-6 with two saves and a 6.47 ERA in 33 contests, including six starts.
Crow, a 24-year-old right-hander, was 4-2 with seven saves and a 4.78 ERA in 33 relief appearances at Triple-A Tacoma.
Villalobos, a 22-year-old third baseman, was hitting .341 with 22 doubles, 11 homers and 53 RBI in 86 games at Class A Lancaster of the California League.
